Ligand 2 is my current best - trifluoromethyl on a cyclopropyl cap, Phi 2.3906 - and ligand 1 the nitrile version just behind it. Ligand 1 is the working molecule: counting its ordering, the nitrile takes atoms 0 and 1, the azine 2 to 6 and 20, the bridge nitrogen 7, the central ring 8 to 12 and 19, and the cap nitrogen 13, carbonyl 14, oxygen 15 with the cyclopropane at 16 to 18. So atom 16 is the ring CH bonded to the carbonyl at 14. I am continuing the aryl series with a pyridin-4-yl. The pyridin-3-yl I built elsewhere this generation puts its nitrogen meta to the biaryl bond; this one puts it para, which is the same mass and the same lipophilicity saving but a different dipole direction and a different position for the acceptor. If both hold the 0.70, the position simply wants a flat ring and I can choose the isomer purely on drug-likeness; if they differ, the ring is making a specific contact and the better isomer is worth building on. Expected product: about 330 Da at LogP near 3.3.
